Supplier.title: Supplier
Supplier.description: Represents a vendor or supplier with whom the business conducts transactions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Supplier entity.

name.description: The official name of the supplier.

cnpj.description: Brazilian National Register of Legal Entities number (CNPJ) of the supplier. (Format: XX.XXX.XXX/XXXX-XX)

contactName.description: Name of the primary contact person at the supplier.

email.description: Email address for contacting the supplier.

phone.description: Phone number for contacting the supplier.

category.description: General category or type of products/services provided by the supplier (e.g., 'Food Ingredients', 'Packaging', 'Utilities').

notes.description: Any additional notes or comments about the supplier.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the supplier record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the supplier record was last updated.

AccountCategory.title: AccountCategory
AccountCategory.description: Defines a category within the chart of accounts, used for classifying financial transactions (e.g., 'Operacional > Insumos > Peixe').

id.description: Unique identifier for the AccountCategory entity.

name.description: The name of the account category (e.g., 'Peixe', 'Aluguel').

description.description: A detailed description of what the category represents.

type.description: The type of financial account, e.g., 'Revenue', 'Expense', 'Asset', 'Liability', 'Equity'.

code.description: An optional alphanumeric code for the account category, useful for hierarchical organization.

parentCategoryId.description: Reference to another AccountCategory entity, establishing a hierarchical relationship. (Relationship: AccountCategory 1:N AccountCategory - self-referencing)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the account category record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the account category record was last updated.

BankAccount.title: BankAccount
BankAccount.description: Stores details about bank accounts used for financial reconciliation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BankAccount entity.

accountName.description: A user-friendly name for the bank account (e.g., 'Main Checking', 'Savings Account').

accountHolderName.description: The name of the account holder as registered with the bank.

initialBalance.description: The initial balance recorded for this account.

currency.description: The currency of the bank account (e.g., 'BRL', 'USD').

description.description: Any additional description for the bank account.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the bank account record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the bank account record was last updated.

AccountsPayableEntry.title: AccountsPayableEntry
AccountsPayableEntry.description: Represents a single entry of an amount owed to a supplier.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AccountsPayableEntry entity.

supplierId.description: Reference to the Supplier to whom the payment is due. (Relationship: Supplier 1:N AccountsPayableEntry)

accountCategoryId.description: Reference to the AccountCategory for classifying this expense. (Relationship: AccountCategory 1:N AccountsPayableEntry)

description.description: A description of the expense or payment reason.

originalAmount.description: The original amount of the expense before any adjustments.

dueDate.description: The date when the payment is due.

interestAmount.description: Any interest applied to the payment.

fineAmount.description: Any fines applied to the payment.

status.description: The current status of the accounts payable entry (e.g., 'Open', 'Paid', 'Overdue').

paymentDate.description: The actual date the payment was made.

paidAmount.description: The total amount actually paid, including interest/fines.

bankAccountId.description: Reference to the BankAccount from which the payment was made. (Relationship: BankAccount 1:N AccountsPayableEntry)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the accounts payable entry was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the accounts payable entry was last updated.

AccountsReceivableEntry.title: AccountsReceivableEntry
AccountsReceivableEntry.description: Represents a single entry of an amount expected to be received by the business.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AccountsReceivableEntry entity.

accountCategoryId.description: Reference to the AccountCategory for classifying this revenue. (Relationship: AccountCategory 1:N AccountsReceivableEntry)

description.description: A description of the revenue or receipt reason.

originalAmount.description: The original amount of revenue expected.

expectedReceiptDate.description: The date when the revenue is expected to be received.

status.description: The current status of the accounts receivable entry (e.g., 'Open', 'Received', 'Overdue').

receiptDate.description: The actual date the revenue was received.

salesChannel.description: The channel through which the revenue was generated (e.g., 'Online', 'In-store', 'Partnership').

bankAccountId.description: Reference to the BankAccount into which the revenue was deposited. (Relationship: BankAccount 1:N AccountsReceivableEntry)

sourceDocumentReference.description: A reference to the original document or report from which this entry was imported.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the accounts receivable entry was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the accounts receivable entry was last updated.

BankTransaction.title: BankTransaction
BankTransaction.description: Represents a single transaction imported from a bank statement (e.g., OFX file) for reconciliation purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BankTransaction entity.

bankAccountId.description: Reference to the BankAccount to which this transaction belongs. (Relationship: BankAccount 1:N BankTransaction)

transactionDate.description: The date the transaction occurred according to the bank statement.

amount.description: The monetary amount of the transaction. Positive for credits, negative for debits.

description.description: The description of the transaction provided by the bank.

type.description: The type of transaction from the bank's perspective (e.g., 'Debit', 'Credit', 'Deposit', 'Withdrawal').

ofxTransactionId.description: A unique identifier for the transaction provided by the OFX file, useful for preventing duplicates.

isMatched.description: Indicates whether this bank transaction has been successfully matched with an Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable entry.

matchedApEntryId.description: Reference to the AccountsPayableEntry if this transaction matches an expense. (Relationship: AccountsPayableEntry 1:N BankTransaction)

matchedArEntryId.description: Reference to the AccountsReceivableEntry if this transaction matches a revenue. (Relationship: AccountsReceivableEntry 1:N BankTransaction)

reconciliationDate.description: The date when this bank transaction was reconciled (matched and confirmed).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the bank transaction record was created (imported).

CashFlowProjection.title: CashFlowProjection
CashFlowProjection.description: Represents a planned or projected cash inflow or outflow for a specific date.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CashFlowProjection entity.

projectionDate.description: The specific date for which this cash flow projection is made.

description.description: A brief description of the projected cash flow item.

type.description: Indicates whether the projection is an 'Inflow' (money coming in) or 'Outflow' (money going out).

amount.description: The projected monetary amount of the cash flow.

isRecurrent.description: Indicates if this projection is for a recurring event.

recurrencePattern.description: Describes the recurrence frequency if 'isRecurrent' is true (e.g., 'Daily', 'Weekly', 'Monthly', 'Yearly').

notes.description: Any additional notes or details about the cash flow projection.

accountCategoryId.description: Reference to the AccountCategory for classifying this projected cash flow. (Relationship: AccountCategory 1:N CashFlowProjection)

bankAccountId.description: Reference to the BankAccount involved in this projection, if specific. (Relationship: BankAccount 1:N CashFlowProjection)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the cash flow projection record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the cash flow projection record was last updated.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure is based on strong user-centric data segregation, adhering strictly to the 'Private Data: Path-Based ownership' and 'Hierarchical Paths for User-Owned Data' mandates. Given that Yumi Yumi 🍣 Finance is designed for personal use, all primary financial entities are nested directly under a specific user's ID. This radical segregation ensures maximum security, simplifies access control, and inherently supports Queryable Access Patterns (QAPs).

**Authorization Independence:** All collections are structured as `/users/{userId}/<collectionName>/{documentId}` or further nested as `/users/{userId}/bankAccounts/{bankAccountId}/bankTransactions/{transactionId}`. This design achieves authorization independence by embedding the `userId` directly into the path of every document. Consequently, security rules will not require any `get()` calls to verify ownership. The rule will simply check if `request.auth.uid == userId` (where `userId` is the wildcard in the path). This makes rules atomic, highly performant, and easy to debug, as authorization is determined solely by the request context and the document's physical location.

**Queryable Access Patterns (QAPs):** The user-scoped structure naturally supports secure `list` operations. Firestore's security rules automatically enforce that `list` queries must include a filter on the `userId` corresponding to the `request.auth.uid` in the path. For instance, a user can only query their own `/users/{request.auth.uid}/suppliers` collection, and attempting to query `/users/anotherUser/suppliers` will be denied. This inherently prevents unauthorized data access during list operations, satisfying the QAPs principle by ensuring rules are not filters, but rather access grants based on path ownership.

**Structural Segregation:** Each collection (`suppliers`, `accountCategories`, `bankAccounts`, `accountsPayableEntries`, `accountsReceivableEntries`, `cashFlowProjections`) under a user's path is designed to hold documents of a single entity type with homogeneous security requirements (i.e., owned by the `userId` in the path). The `bankTransactions` collection is further segregated under specific `bankAccounts` to reflect their natural hierarchical relationship while maintaining the same user-ownership security posture.

**Denormalization:** In this user-specific context, explicit denormalization of authorization context is largely unnecessary as the `userId` in the path serves as the ultimate authorization context for all documents within that user's scope. Data references (e.g., `supplierId` in `AccountsPayableEntry`) are internal logical links, not authorization dependencies, as the linked `Supplier` entity is also owned by the same `userId`.
